title: Advanced fuzzing (Sebastian Schulze, 2014 GSoC)
description: The 2014 advanced fuzzing project in the Student Hall of Fame next to the multi-fuzz commits, the 2015 merge into the fuzz add-on, and where it stands now.
narrative:
A tester who wants to try many values in one request field is probably glad of a tool that sends them automatically. The Student Hall of Fame lists Advanced fuzzing (Sebastian Schulze) as a 2014 Summer GSoC project. The project wiki's goals include "Development of a stable HTTP - multifuzzing add-on".

In June 2014 a core commit added packages for multi-fuzzing. A zap-extensions commit of the same day updated the multi-fuzz add-on. Later that month a commit added a new dialog layout, script payloads and regular expression payloads, and made the single-fuzzing package permanently available.

In April 2015 a commit removed the multi-fuzz add-on. Commits of April 2015 for issue 1434 merged the fuzzer with MultiFuzz and moved the result into an add-on.

The fuzz add-on was moved into a project of its own in April 2019. The fuzz add-on is still in zap-extensions. A commit of August 2026 fixed breadth-first handling. The CHANGELOG for version 13.17.0, dated August 2026, lists a fix to breadth-first Pitchfork payload replacement when fuzzing multiple locations. It also renames the strategies to Cluster Bomb and Pitchfork, which were previously Depth First and Breadth First. Those names probably match the terms testers meet in other fuzzing tools.

chapters.title: June 2014: multi-fuzzing in core and as an add-on
chapters.text: The Student Hall of Fame lists Advanced fuzzing (Sebastian Schulze) as a 2014 Summer GSoC project. The wiki goals include "Development of a stable HTTP - multifuzzing add-on" and "Inclusion of scripts as payload resources". A zaproxy commit by BastiSchulze dated 2014-06-04 is titled "Core packages for multi-fuzzing." A zap-extensions commit dated the same day begins "Updated multi-fuzz add-on."

chapters.title: Summer 2014: payloads and scripts
chapters.text: Commits by BastiSchulze in zaproxy include "Changed label for fuzzing entry in right-click popup-menu." (2014-06-06) and one dated 2014-06-23 that begins "New dialog layout, script payloads, regEx payloads and permanent availability of the single-fuzzing package". The matching zap-extensions commit of 2014-06-23 has the same beginning.

chapters.title: April 2015: merged into one add-on
chapters.text: A zap-extensions commit dated 2015-04-12 is titled "Remove multiFuzz add-on (Issue 1434)". Commits dated 2015-04-13 include "Issue 1434 - Merge Fuzzer with MultiFuzz and move the result to an add-on" in zap-extensions and "Remove fuzzers, pre-merge changes (Issue 1434)" in zaproxy.

chapters.title: 2019 to now
chapters.text: "fuzz: relocate to its own project" is dated 2019-04-03. The fuzz add-on is still in zap-extensions; the latest commit touching addOns/fuzz is dated 2026-10-05 ("Update localized resources"). The commit "fuzz: Fix breadth first handling" is dated 2026-08-04. The CHANGELOG for 13.17.0 (2026-08-07) lists under Fixed "Correct (breadth-first) Pitchfork payload replacement when fuzzing multiple locations." and under Changed "Rename payload replacement strategies to Cluster Bomb and Pitchfork in the UI and help (previously Depth First and Breadth First)."
